claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6H and Figure 6—figure supplement 1E.

claims.claim: Knockdown of p73α/γ led to reduction in Leptin expression in isogenic control cells in that p73α is the predominant isoform.
claims.source: Interestingly, knockdown of p73α/γ also led to reduction in Leptin expression in isogenic control cells in that p73α is the predominant isoform (Figure 6H and Figure 6—figure supplement 1E), suggesting that p73α can regulate Leptin transcription.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6H and Figure 6—figure supplement 1E.

claims.claim: Ectopic expression of TAp73α, TAp73β, or TAp73γ alone was able to induce Leptin expression, with the strongest induction by TAp73γ.
claims.source: To further test this, we found that ectopic expression of TAp73α, TAp73β, or TAp73γ alone was able to induce Leptin expression, with the strongest induction by TAp73γ (Figure 6—figure supplement 1F).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1F.

claims.claim: A potential p73 response element (p73-RE) is located at nt –346 to –321 in the Leptin promoter.
claims.source: To determine whether Leptin is a direct target of TAp73, we searched the Leptin promoter and found a potential p73 response element (p73-RE) located at nt –346 to –321 (Figure 6I).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on bioinformatic analysis of the Leptin promoter sequence.

claims.claim: Ectopic TAp73γ was able to bind to the LEP promoter.
claims.source: Thus, ChIP assay was performed and showed that ectopic TAp73γ was able to bind to the LEP promoter (Figure 6J).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from ChIP assay shown in Figure 6J.

claims.claim: Endogenous p73γ were able to bind to the Leptin promoter in E11-KO H1299 cells compared to isogenic control cells.
claims.source: Consistent with this, endogenous p73γ were able to bind to the Leptin promoter in E11-KO H1299 cells compared to isogenic control cells (Figure 6K and L).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from ChIP assay shown in Figure 6K and L.

claims.claim: TAp73α/β/γ were able to activate the Leptin-WT reporter, with the strongest activation by TAp73γ.
claims.source: We found that TAp73α/β/γ were able to activate the Leptin-WT reporter, with the strongest activation by TAp73γ (Figure 6M).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from luciferase assay shown in Figure 6M.

claims.claim: All TAp73 isoforms were unable to transactivate the luciferase reporter containing mutant p73-RE.
claims.source: By contrast, all TAp73 isoforms were unable to transactivate the luciferase reporter containing mutant p73-RE (Figure 6M).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from luciferase assay shown in Figure 6M.

claims.claim: Knockdown of Leptin abrogated the elevated level of cholesterol and triglycerides by E11-KO in both H1299 and Mia-PaCa2 cells.
claims.source: We showed that knockdown of Leptin abrogated the elevated level of cholesterol and triglycerides by E11-KO in both H1299 and Mia-PaCa2 cells (Figure 7B and C and Figure 7—figure supplement 1B and C), consistent with the observation that knockdown of p73γ also abrogated the elevated level of cholesterol and triglycerides by E11-KO (Figure 5M and N and Figure 5—figure supplement 1C and D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7B, C and Figure 7—figure supplement 1B, C.

claims.claim: In isogenic control cells, cell migration was moderately inhibited by knockdown of Leptin in both H1299 and Mia-PaCa2 cells.
claims.source: Next, we examined the role of Leptin in cell migration and showed that in isogenic control cells, cell migration was moderately inhibited by knockdown of Leptin in both H1299 (Figure 7D and E and Figure 7—figure supplement 1D) and Mia-PaCa2 cells (Figure 7—figure supplement 1E and F).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7D, E and Figure 7—figure supplement 1D, E, F.

claims.claim: The enhanced cell migration by E11-KO was abolished by knockdown of Leptin in both H1299 and Mia-PaCa2 cells.
claims.source: By contrast, the enhanced cell migration by E11-KO was abolished by knockdown of Leptin in both H1299 (Figure 7D and E and Figure 7—figure supplement 1D) and Mia-PaCa2 cells (Figure 7—figure supplement 1E and F), consistent with the observation that knockdown of p73γ also abolished the enhanced cell migration by E11-KO (Figure 3C and Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7D, E and Figure 7—figure supplement 1D, E, F.

claims.claim: LepR was expressed at a similar level across isogenic control, TAp73-KO and E11-KO H1299 cells.
claims.source: We found that LepR was expressed at a similar level across isogenic control, TAp73-KO and E11-KO H1299 cells (Figure 7—figure supplement 1G), suggesting that these cells have an intact Leptin signaling pathway and that LepR expression is not regulated by p73.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1G.

claims.claim: Cell transmigration was enhanced by treatment with Leptin in isogenic control, TAp73-KO and E11-KO H1299 cells.
claims.source: Importantly, we found that cell transmigration was enhanced by treatment with Leptin in isogenic control, TAp73-KO and E11-KO H1299 cells (Figure 7—figure supplement 1H).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1H.

claims.source: We found that Leptin expression was low in normal human prostates but highly elevated in prostate carcinomas, which correlates well with the expression of p73γ (Figure 7F and G, Leptin and p73γ panels, compare lanes 1–5 with 6–13).

claims.source: Similarly, Leptin and p73γ transcripts were found to be highly expressed coordinately in dog lymphomas compared to normal dog lymph nodes (Figure 7H, Leptin and p73γ panels, compare lanes 1–3 with 4–19).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7H.

claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from xenograft assay shown in Figure 8A.

claims.source: Notably, we found that treatment with p73γ or Leptin siRNA led to extensive tumor necrosis in xenografts compared with that treated with the control scrambled siRNA (Figure 8J).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8J.

claims.claim: Leptin is a direct target of TAp73.
claims.source: Together, these data indicate that Leptin is a novel target of TAp73γ and may play a role in TAp73γ-induced oncogenic activities.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on multiple lines of experimental evidence including ChIP assay and luciferase reporter assay.

claims.claim: p73α and p73γ have opposing functions in tumorigenesis.
claims.source: These results have provided compelling evidence and prompted us to hypothesize that p73 C-terminal isoforms, that is, TAp73α and TAp73γ, can exert two opposing functions in tumorigenesis in a manner similar to that by TA and ΔN p73 isoforms.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on inference from multiple experimental observations throughout the study.

claims.source: Together, these data suggest that TAp73γ is primarily responsible for the enhanced cell proliferation and migration observed in E11-KO cells.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on inference from multiple experimental observations including knockdown and overexpression studies.

claims.claim: E11-deficient mice phenocopies Trp73-deficient mice with short lifespan, infertility, and chronic inflammation.
claims.source: Additionally, we found that E11-deficient mice phenocopies Trp73-deficient mice with short lifespan, infertility, and chronic inflammation.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on experimental observations from mouse studies.

claims.claim: The p73γ-Leptin pathway promotes tumorigenesis and alters lipid metabolism.
claims.source: Our study indicates that the p73γ-Leptin pathway promotes tumorigenesis and alters lipid metabolism, which may be targeted for cancer management.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on inference from multiple experimental observations throughout the study.

results.result: The authors demonstrate that p73α to p73γ isoform switching occurs in human cancers and dog lymphomas. Analysis of TCGA data shows increased exon 11 exclusion in lung and head-neck squamous cell carcinomas compared to normal tissues (C26, C27). In human prostate carcinomas, p73α is lost while p73γ is elevated compared to normal prostates (C28, C29). Similarly, in dog lymphomas, p73α is undetectable while p73γ is elevated compared to normal lymph nodes (C31, C32).
results.evaluation: Claims C26-C32 provide converging evidence from multiple tissue types (human lung, head-neck, prostate cancers and dog lymphomas) showing consistent p73α to p73γ isoform switching. The data includes both bioinformatic analysis (TCGA) and experimental measurements (RT-PCR) with appropriate controls (normal tissues). Sample sizes appear adequate (n=5 normal prostates, n=16 prostate carcinomas; n=3 normal lymph nodes, n=16 lymphomas).

results.result: CRISPR-mediated deletion of the E11 splicing acceptor in TP73 successfully triggers exon 11 skipping and results in isoform switching from p73α to p73γ. E11-KO cells show loss of α/β isoforms, increased γ/ε isoforms, and unchanged δ/ζ isoforms compared to isogenic controls (C34). TA/ΔNp73 isoforms remain at similar levels (C35), and TAp73γ becomes the predominant isoform in E11-KO cells while TAp73α is predominant in controls (C36).
results.evaluation: Claims C33-C36 demonstrate successful genetic manipulation to model the isoform switch observed in cancers. The experimental design is sound with appropriate isogenic controls, and multiple detection methods (RT-PCR, Western blot with specific antibodies) confirm the isoform switch at both transcript and protein levels. The data in Figure 2A-C support these claims.

results.result: E11 deficiency promotes oncogenic phenotypes in vitro. E11-KO cells show enhanced colony formation compared to TAp73-KO cells (C37-C39), increased cell migration compared to all other cell lines including TAp73-KO (C40-C43), and aberrant epithelial morphogenesis with irregular acini and filled lumen similar to TAp73-KO cells (C46).
results.evaluation: Claims C37-C43, C46 are well-supported by multiple complementary assays (colony formation, scratch assay, transwell migration, 3D culture) across multiple cell lines (H1299, Mia-PaCa2, MCF10A). The inclusion of TAp73-KO, ΔNp73-KO, and isogenic controls allows proper comparison. The finding that E11-KO shows stronger oncogenic effects than TAp73-KO is particularly notable and well-documented.

results.result: TAp73γ is primarily responsible for the oncogenic effects observed in E11-KO cells. Inducible expression of TAp73γ promotes cell migration (C47). Knockdown of p73α/γ has opposite effects in control versus E11-KO cells: it enhances migration and tumor sphere viability in controls but decreases them in E11-KO cells (C48-C50). ΔNp73/E11 double knockout does not alter migration compared to E11-KO alone (C51), indicating TAp73γ can overcome ΔNp73 deficiency effects (C52).
results.evaluation: Claims C47-C52, C110 provide strong evidence through gain-of-function (inducible TAp73γ) and loss-of-function (siRNA knockdown, double knockout) approaches. The opposite effects of p73α/γ knockdown in control versus E11-KO cells elegantly demonstrate that p73α (predominant in controls) suppresses while p73γ (predominant in E11-KO) promotes oncogenic phenotypes. The double knockout experiment (C51) provides additional genetic evidence.

results.result: E11-deficient mice recapitulate key phenotypes of Trp73-deficient mice but show distinct tumor spectrum. E11 deficiency causes isoform switching in MEFs (C53), reduced cellular senescence (C54), and in E11-KO mice causes runty phenotype, infertility, and hydrocephalus (C55). E11-HET mice show shortened lifespan similar to Trp73+/- mice (C56), increased tumor incidence (C57), but significantly higher percentage of DLBCL (50% vs 14.8%) (C58). Both genotypes show chronic inflammation (C59-C60) and various hyperplasias (C61-C64), though with some differences in severity and tissue distribution.
results.evaluation: Claims C53-C64, C111 are supported by comprehensive in vivo analysis with adequate sample sizes (n=51 WT, n=27 Trp73+/-, n=28 E11-HET mice). Statistical analysis is appropriate (Fisher's exact test, log-rank test). The finding that E11-HET mice show higher DLBCL incidence than Trp73+/- mice (p=0.009) is particularly significant and suggests a specific role for p73γ in B-cell lymphomagenesis. However, the use of historical controls for WT and some Trp73+/- mice is a limitation.

results.result: E11 deficiency leads to obesity and altered lipid metabolism. E11-HET mice show enlarged adipocytes (C65), increased VAT mass (C66), liver steatosis (C67), elevated liver enzyme transcripts (C68), and increased serum cholesterol and triglycerides at both old (~65 weeks) and young (20-32 weeks) ages (C69-C72). In vitro, E11-KO cells show increased cholesterol and triglycerides that is reversed by p73γ knockdown (C73-C74), while p73α/γ knockdown in control cells increases lipid levels (C75).
results.evaluation: Claims C65-C75 provide strong evidence through multiple complementary approaches (histology, serum measurements, in vitro assays) with appropriate controls. The in vitro rescue experiments (C74) and the opposite effect of knockdown in control cells (C75) strengthen the conclusion that p73γ promotes while p73α inhibits lipid storage. Sample sizes appear adequate (n=3 per group for most measurements). The phenotype is observed at multiple ages, suggesting it is not merely age-related.

results.result: Leptin is a direct transcriptional target of p73 isoforms, with strongest induction by TAp73γ. E11-HET mice show adipose tissue inflammation (C76), increased proinflammatory cytokines (C77), and elevated Leptin in tissues and serum (C78-C81). Leptin expression is markedly increased in E11-HET compared to Trp73+/- mice (C82). In cells, TAp73 and E11-KO increase Leptin while ΔNp73-KO has little effect (C83-C85). Ectopic TAp73γ induces Leptin (C86, C89), while p73γ knockdown reduces it in E11-KO cells (C87). Both p73α and p73γ can regulate Leptin, with p73γ being strongest (C88-C89, C108).
results.evaluation: Claims C76-C89, C108 establish Leptin as a p73 target through multiple lines of evidence: correlation in vivo (C76-C82), genetic manipulation in cells (C83-C89), and the claim of direct targeting (C108) is supported by subsequent mechanistic studies (C90-C94). The dose-response relationship (E11-HET > Trp73+/- > WT) and the differential effects of p73 isoforms are well-documented. However, C108 requires additional mechanistic evidence from subsequent claims to be fully supported.

results.result: Leptin is a direct transcriptional target of TAp73 through a specific p73 response element. A putative p73-RE is located at nt -346 to -321 in the Leptin promoter (C90). ChIP assays demonstrate that both ectopic TAp73γ (C91) and endogenous p73γ in E11-KO cells (C92) bind to the Leptin promoter. Luciferase reporter assays show that TAp73α/β/γ activate the wild-type Leptin promoter, with strongest activation by TAp73γ (C93), but cannot activate a reporter with mutant p73-RE (C94).
results.evaluation: Claims C90-C94 provide strong mechanistic evidence for direct transcriptional regulation through complementary approaches: bioinformatic identification of the response element (C90), ChIP assays demonstrating binding (C91-C92), and functional validation through luciferase assays (C93-C94). The mutation of the p73-RE abolishing transactivation (C94) is particularly strong evidence for specificity. These claims together support the conclusion that Leptin is a direct target.

results.result: Leptin mediates the oncogenic effects of TAp73γ. Knockdown of Leptin abolishes the elevated cholesterol/triglycerides (C95) and enhanced cell migration (C96-C97) caused by E11-KO. LepR is expressed at similar levels across cell lines (C98), and exogenous Leptin treatment enhances cell transmigration (C99). In human prostate carcinomas and dog lymphomas, Leptin expression correlates with p73γ expression (C100-C101).
results.evaluation: Claims C95-C101 demonstrate that Leptin is functionally important for p73γ-mediated effects through loss-of-function (siRNA) and gain-of-function (exogenous Leptin) approaches. The correlation between Leptin and p73γ in clinical samples (C100-C101) provides translational relevance. The finding that LepR is not regulated by p73 (C98) is important for interpreting the Leptin treatment experiments. The data support Leptin as a critical mediator.

results.result: Targeting p73γ or Leptin suppresses E11-KO xenograft tumor growth. E11-KO cells form larger tumors than control cells (C102-C103) with elevated p73γ and Leptin (C104). Intratumoral injection of siRNAs against p73γ or Leptin significantly reduces tumor growth rate (C105), tumor size and weight (C106), and causes extensive tumor necrosis (C107).
results.evaluation: Claims C102-C107 provide strong in vivo validation of therapeutic potential. The experimental design includes appropriate controls (scrambled siRNA) and adequate sample sizes (n=6-7 per group). Statistical significance is demonstrated (p<0.05). The extensive tumor necrosis (C107) is a particularly striking phenotype. However, the use of transient transfection followed by injection and one additional intratumoral injection may not fully represent sustained knockdown, which is a limitation for therapeutic interpretation.

results.result: The authors propose that p73α and p73γ have opposing functions in tumorigenesis, and that the p73γ-Leptin pathway promotes tumorigenesis and alters lipid metabolism. This represents a novel paradigm where C-terminal p73 isoforms (p73α vs p73γ) have opposing roles similar to N-terminal isoforms (TAp73 vs ΔNp73).
results.evaluation: Claims C109 and C112 represent the major conclusions synthesized from all experimental results. The evidence from multiple experimental systems (cell lines, mouse models, clinical samples) consistently shows that p73α suppresses while p73γ promotes oncogenic phenotypes, lipid accumulation, and Leptin expression. The mechanistic link through Leptin is well-established. These conclusions are well-supported by the totality of the data, though they represent interpretive synthesis rather than single experimental findings.

results.result: The authors provide comprehensive background on TP73 gene structure, p73 isoforms, and their known functions. This includes chromosomal location (C1), similarity to p53 (C2-C3), mutation frequency (C4), biological functions (C5), promoter usage generating TA and ΔN isoforms (C6-C8), mouse phenotypes (C9-C10), context-dependent activities (C11), and C-terminal splicing variants (C12-C18).
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C18 are background information supported by appropriate citations to published literature. These establish the scientific context for the study but do not represent new findings. The claims accurately represent established knowledge about p73 biology based on the citations provided.

results.result: The authors provide background on Leptin biology, including its structure and production (C19), role in energy homeostasis (C20), anti-obesity effects in congenital deficiency (C21), leptin resistance in common obesity (C22), pleiotropic functions (C23), role in cancer progression (C24), and alterations in obesity-associated cancers (C25).
results.evaluation: Claims C19-C25 are background information supported by appropriate citations to published literature. These establish the rationale for investigating Leptin as a potential mediator of p73γ effects but do not represent new findings. The claims accurately represent established knowledge about Leptin biology.

results.result: In 3D culture, parental and isogenic control MCF10A cells form normal acini with hollow lumen (C44), while ΔNp73-KO cells show delayed acinus formation with small acini (C45).
results.evaluation: Claims C44-C45 are supported by the 3D culture data in Figure 2G. These serve as controls for the E11-KO and TAp73-KO phenotypes (C46) and demonstrate that ΔNp73 has a distinct role in epithelial morphogenesis. The data are clear and appropriately controlled.
